hook_text: In Paper 2 geometry, a CORRECT answer with no reason scores zero. The marks are paid in words.
clip_script: Euclidean geometry pays its forty marks in a currency of reasons: every statement in a proof earns only when its reason is stated in the accepted wording. A central angle of one hundred degrees forces fifty degrees at the circumference on the same arc — reason, angle at centre equals two times angle at circumference. A diameter whispers ninety degrees, a tangent whispers tan-chord, a cyclic quadrilateral whispers supplementary. Read the diagram and mark everything given, because each given is a theorem invitation — and the proof is the corridor where the givens and the target meet.
visual_style: A bank teller's counter where geometric statements slide across and get stamped PAID only when a reason card accompanies them; circle diagrams lighting up as each given whispers its theorem in glowing script.
mood: Confident insider knowledge — the rulebook the markers actually use.
pacing: Crisp stamp-by-stamp rhythm, a whispered-theorem montage, firm close on the corridor line.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision lesson and learn the exact wording the memo pays for.
